messages.content:
Implement one complete standalone child-facing HTML evaluation from the immutable academic and design artifacts.

Implement the artifacts faithfully. You own implementation details needed to make the declared interaction work, but you may not add another design doctrine, change academic content, expose an answer before the first committed response, or make learning conclusions.

The document must work at the declared viewport with touch and mouse and no keyboard requirement. The child must always be able to continue after an incorrect, uncertain, or instrument-ambiguous response. Every queried DOM element must exist before JavaScript accesses it. Use no parent application endpoints, cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, currency, browser speech synthesis, or oscillator audio.

Post evaluation_ready, evaluation_attempt, evaluation_friction, and evaluation_complete messages to window.parent. Every attempt must include itemId, constructId, result, assistance, exposure, responseMode, possibleConfounds, and attemptedValue. Return one complete HTML document and nothing else.

TARGET VIEWPORT
1365×768

{
  "artifactId": "DESIGN-EVAL-LAB-MATH-C-OPEN-01-juniper-v1",
  "upstreamHash": "274c49ed00318c3c5e7eb4fae53bfbbea61645b4488f4b88780ba9cb431b7361",
  "title": "Four Quiet Questions: an equal-groups evidence session with neutral countable shapes",
  "designRationale": "The contract prohibits narrative, game mechanics, themes, sound, and rewards, and demands that each item collect an independent response before any support. My job is therefore not to entertain but to make the honest state of this child's understanding legible. The design centers on one commitment: every pixel on screen either presents the stimulus, presents the response affordance, or gets out of the way. The child evidence (asks for harder problems, questions faulty logic, requests hints when stuck) is treated strictly as hypothesis: she may tolerate the ITEM-4 discrimination well, and she may stall rather than guess. That second hypothesis drives the most important affordance decision — 'Not sure' is a first-class, equally sized, always-visible response, styled with the same visual weight as numeric answers, so stalling becomes recorded missing evidence rather than a forced error or an abandoned session. The small-sample feedback favoring hints is explicitly overridden during the evidence window per the contract; the hint affordance appears only on the closing screen, after all four outcomes are recorded, and any post-window hint interaction is logged separately. Response modes are the contract's own: large tap-target number chips (1–10) for numeric fields and large option cards for selections, so neither typing, reading fluency, nor pointer precision can masquerade as mathematical evidence. Each screen shows exactly one stimulus, one short sentence, and one response area; the required first action is always answerable from what is visible. Nothing confirms or denies correctness at any point in the session; the confirm control advances with identical, affectively neutral motion regardless of what was answered. Color is used to separate stimulus from response zones, never to differentiate groups within a stimulus in a way that could pre-chunk the counting for her or leak the answer.",
  "independentlyChosenPrinciples": [
    "Evidence before comfort: no feedback, hints, examples, or answer exposure until all four outcomes are recorded; the child's first response to each item is the only response.",
    "'Not sure' has equal dignity: it is rendered at the same size, position class, and visual weight as substantive answers on every item, and confirming it advances identically, so choosing it never feels like failing.",
    "Answer chips, not keyboards: all numeric responses are made by tapping one chip from a 1–10 row of 64px minimum targets; no text field, no keyboard, no drag, no draw.",
    "One screen, one decision: each screen contains exactly one stimulus, one sentence of at most twelve words, and one response region; nothing else is interactive.",
    "Neutral affect throughout: identical transition motion, identical confirm behavior, and no evaluative color, icon, sound, or copy after any response, correct or not, so the child cannot read correctness off the instrument.",
    "Color separates zones, never answers: stimulus dots/squares are a single uniform color; color contrast distinguishes the stimulus panel from the response panel but never encodes group boundaries, counts, or correct options.",
    "Reversibility until commit: any chip or card can be re-tapped or changed freely before the single explicit Confirm; only the confirmed state is recorded as the independent response, and pre-confirm changes are logged as friction data, not answers.",

  "openingState": "The session opens on a single calm screen: an off-white background, a centered short line in large child-legible type — 'Four questions about groups. Optionally-available speaker icons for read-aloud of on-screen sentences are present next to each sentence throughout (see interactionModel); tapping one reads the sentence only, never any answer content, and its use is logged as a reading-support event, not as a hint. There is no character, no score display, no progress bar with celebratory framing — only four small neutral dots across the top indicating position in the sequence (filled = answered or resolved as not-sure/omitted, hollow = upcoming), so the child always knows how much remains without any evaluative meaning attached. Tapping Start transitions directly to ITEM-1's screen: on the left ~60% of the width, the stimulus panel shows four clearly separated clusters of six uniform dots on a subtly tinted panel; on the right, the response panel shows the prompt sentence, then two labeled answer rows ('How many bunches?' with chips 1–10, 'How many dots in each bunch?' with chips 1–10), a 'Not sure' card of equal visual weight, and a Confirm button that remains inactive until both fields have a selection or 'Not sure' is selected.",
  "firstAction": "The first required action after Start is: look at the four clusters of dots and tap one number chip in the 'How many bunches?' row. No instructions, tutorial, or example precede it — the contract forbids worked examples, and the interaction is self-evidencing: a tapped chip visibly fills, showing the child her selection registered.",
  "interactionModel": "Touch-first, mouse-equivalent, zero keyboard. Global grammar across all four items: (1) inspect the stimulus panel; (2) tap answer affordances in the response panel — number chips for numeric fields, option cards for selections; (3) selections highlight with a filled state and can be changed freely by tapping a different chip/card; (4) tap Confirm exactly once to record and advance. Confirm is disabled (visibly muted) until every required field on the item has either a value or 'Not sure' selected, preventing accidental empty submissions while never blocking a deliberate 'Not sure'. Per-item specifics: ITEM-1 and ITEM-2 use two labeled chip rows (groups/per-group; rows/per-row) plus a whole-item 'Not sure' card that clears and disables the chip rows when selected (tappable again to un-select). ITEM-3 shows the five groups of three on the left and four equation cards plus a 'Not sure' card stacked on the right; equation option order is randomized per session to control position bias, and the randomization seed is logged. ITEM-4 shows Statement A and Statement B in two visually parallel boxes (A above B, order fixed per contract stimulus, order noted as a logged potential anchor confound); below them, three cards — 'Same situation', 'Different situations', 'Not sure' — and then a second field, 'How many baskets in Statement A?' with chips 1–10 plus its own 'Not sure' chip. Read-aloud: every on-screen sentence and every equation card has a small speaker icon that plays a recorded human reading of exactly that text (equations read as symbols: 'five times three equals fifteen'); this mitigates the reading confound the contract flags, especially for ITEM-4, without teaching, because it only voices what is already printed. Each read-aloud tap is timestamped and logged. 'Stop' opens a two-option confirm ('Keep going' / 'Stop now') to prevent accidental exits; stopping goes to the closing screen.",
  "responseAffordances": "Numeric fields: a single horizontal row of ten chips labeled 1–10, minimum 64×64px, minimum 12px gutters, high-contrast numerals — one tap selects, tapping another chip moves the selection, tapping the selected chip deselects. This preserves the mathematics (the child must produce each quantity herself, in the correct labeled role) while eliminating typing, spelling, and precision confounds; the 1–10 range exactly matches the contract's factor range so the affordance itself leaks nothing. Selections: option cards with full-card tap targets (minimum 88px tall), rendered in identical neutral style; the correct option is never distinguished by position (randomized on ITEM-3), size, or color. 'Not sure': on every item, rendered as a card of the same family — same border weight, same corner radius, slightly different fill tint so it is discoverable but not stigmatized — labeled 'Not sure' with a small tilted-question-mark glyph. Confirm: one wide button per screen labeled 'Done', identical on all items. Field labels are placed immediately above their own chip rows and mirror the stimulus vocabulary exactly ('bunches', 'rows', 'baskets') so the role of each field is unambiguous — this matters most because role-reversal is a scored diagnostic outcome and must reflect the child's structural reading, not label ambiguity. Nothing on any screen accepts free text.",
  "progression": "Fixed contract sequence: ITEM-1 (C1, dot clusters 4×6) → ITEM-2 (C3, array 3×7) → ITEM-3 (C2, equation match 5×3) → ITEM-4 (C4, referent swap 2×8). One stimulus per screen; no back navigation after Confirm, because a recorded independent response must not be revisable after later items could inform it — this is stated to the child implicitly by the forward-only motion and the position dots, not by warning text. Between items, a 400ms neutral crossfade with no interstitial copy, no 'nice job', no summary. Pacing is entirely child-controlled: no timer, no idle prompts that could function as pressure; if the screen is idle for a long period the instrument does nothing visible but logs the idle span as possible stall data. Note on ITEM-2/ITEM-3 ordering: the contract's completionRule sequence lists ITEM-2 (the array/C3 item) before ITEM-3 (the equation/C2 item), and I preserve that literal item order exactly; its stated rationale (later items must not reveal structure needed by earlier ones) holds because the equation options in ITEM-3 expose symbolic multiplication only after both pure-representation items are already recorded. ITEM-4 comes last so the sharpest discrimination is never previewed. After ITEM-4's Confirm (or after an early Stop), the closing screen appears and the evidence window formally closes.",
  "feedbackAndRecovery": "During the evidence window there is exactly one kind of feedback: interaction acknowledgment. A tapped chip fills; a tapped card gains a border; Confirm depresses and the screen advances. No correctness signal of any kind — no color shift, no sound, no icon, no delayed tell (transition motion and timing are identical for every possible answer, including 'Not sure', so the instrument is unreadable as an answer oracle). Recovery paths: (1) mis-taps are recoverable before Confirm by re-tapping, and every pre-confirm change is logged as a change event with timestamps (friction/uncertainty data, never scored); (2) uncertainty is recoverable via 'Not sure', which is always sufficient to enable Confirm and always advances normally; (3) fatigue or refusal is recoverable via 'Stop', which after a two-option confirmation records remaining items as missing evidence and shows the same closing screen as full completion — an early stop is never visually distinguishable as failure; (4) accidental double-taps on Confirm are debounced; (5) if the child triggers read-aloud, it can be replayed without limit and never blocks input. There are no error states the child can reach: no field validation messages, no wrong-input rejections, no dead ends. The only post-window affordance is on the closing screen: a quiet 'Want a hint about any of these later?' toggle that, if tapped, is recorded as post-window hint interest and handed to the follow-up phase — no hint content is delivered inside this instrument at all, keeping even post-window exposure at zero within this artifact.",
  "visualSystem": "Palette: warm off-white background (#F7F5F0), deep slate text (#2B3440), stimulus panel on a very light blue-gray tint (#EBF0F4), response panel on the base background — the tint difference marks 'look here' vs 'answer here' and nothing else. All countable shapes are a single uniform mid-blue (#3A6EA5): dots are identical filled circles, array squares are identical filled squares with 2px white gaps (gaps aid one-to-one counting without labeling rows), ITEM-3's group items are identical circles. No shape within a stimulus varies in color, size, or decoration, honoring the prohibition on art direction beyond neutral countable shapes and the rule that grouping cues must not signal answers. Cluster separation in ITEM-1 uses generous whitespace only (each cluster's internal dot spacing tight, inter-cluster spacing at least 3× internal spacing) so cluster boundaries are unmistakable at 1365×768 without outlines that would pre-count groups for her. The 3×7 array renders with square cells large enough (~56px) that off-by-one visual scanning errors are minimized at this viewport. Typography: a round humanist sans at 28px+ for prompts, 32px for chip numerals, high contrast, maximum twelve words per sentence, no italics, no all-caps. Selected states use a saturated fill of the same blue family plus a 3px outline — a state change, not a reward color. Nothing flashes, nothing animates decoratively, no illustrations, no mascots. Layout is identical across items (stimulus left, response right; ITEM-4 substitutes the two statement boxes for the picture) so the child never re-learns the screen.",
  "motionSystem": "Motion exists only to confirm input and mark transitions, never to evaluate. Chip/card selection: 120ms ease-out fill, no bounce. Confirm press: 80ms depress. Screen transition: 400ms crossfade, identical duration and easing after every answer type so motion carries zero correctness information. Position dots at top fill with a 150ms fade as items resolve. Read-aloud icon pulses gently only while audio is playing, as a 'sound is coming from here' indicator. No parallax, no particle effects, no celebratory motion anywhere, including the closing screen. All motion respects a static fallback: if the platform signals reduced motion, transitions become instant cuts with no functional loss.",
  "soundSystem": "The contract prohibits sound, music, and reward audio; the sound system is therefore silent by default with exactly one permitted audio channel: child-initiated read-aloud of printed on-screen text via the speaker icons, included solely to control the reading-load confound the contract itself flags for ITEM-1's sentence and especially ITEM-4's two statements. Recorded human voice, flat instructional tone, reads only the literal printed words (equations read symbolically), never paraphrases, never emphasizes any option differently — all four ITEM-3 equation cards are recorded with matched prosody so intonation cannot leak the answer. No tap sounds, no transition sounds, no completion sound. Every read-aloud invocation is logged with item, target text, and timestamp so analysts can see whether evidence was gathered with or without reading support.",
  "completionPayoff": "The closing screen is deliberately modest, matching the prohibition on rewards, points, and badges: the four position dots shown filled (or partially filled after an early stop), and one factual line — 'You answered these four questions. That's all for now.' with 'answered' softened to 'looked at' when items were stopped or not-sure. No stars, no score, no correct-count, no confetti, no mastery language, and critically no per-item correctness reveal, since answer exposure is prohibited inside this instrument. Two quiet affordances: 'All done' (closes the session) and the optional post-window 'Want a hint about any of these later?' toggle described above, which records interest without delivering content. The payoff for the child is closure and respect — a clear, unambiguous ending with no judgment. The payoff for the accountable system is a clean evidence record: four outcomes, each from the set {correct, incorrect, not_sure, omitted, abandoned}, with confound flags, latencies, change events, read-aloud events, and completion status.",

  "measurementResponsibilities": "The instrument records, per item: the confirmed response (mapped to {correct, incorrect, not_sure, omitted, abandoned} against the immutable correct-answer contracts), all contract measurement keys (c1_group_pair_correct, c1_roles_reversed, c1_reported_total_instead_of_pair [inferred, see instrumentRisks], c1_not_sure_rate, c3_array_dimensions_correct, c3_roles_reversed, c3_reported_total_instead_of_dimensions, c3_off_by_one_count, c3_not_sure_rate, c2_equation_match_correct, c2_additive_distractor_selected, c2_duplicated_factor_distractor_selected, c2_product_only_recognition_flag, c2_not_sure_rate, c2_selection_latency_below_inspection_threshold, c4_referent_discrimination_correct, c4_same_selected_product_equality_confusion, c4_referent_count_correct, c4_ambiguity_flag_requires_followup, c4_not_sure_rate), and all latency keys (time to first entry/selection/response per item), while explicitly excluding from scoring: reading time, keystroke count (none exist), pointer path length, pointer precision, and typing speed. Additional factual telemetry: pre-confirm change events with timestamps (friction/uncertainty, unscored), idle spans (stall data), read-aloud invocations per text target (reading-support exposure), ITEM-3 option-order seed, Stop invocations and confirmations, and post-window hint-interest toggle state. Assistance exposure during the evidence window is reported as a constant: none — no hints, examples, feedback, or answer exposure occurred, by construction. Confound gating is applied exactly per contract: sub-threshold-latency correct responses downgrade to evidence_ambiguous; any item flagged for reading, input, or pointer interference downgrades to evidence_ambiguous; every ITEM-4 'same' response is flagged evidence_ambiguous pending the disambiguation probe. Cross-item consistency checks (dual role-reversal on ITEM-1/ITEM-2; correct ITEM-3 with incorrect ITEM-1/ITEM-2 as probable product recognition) are computed and attached. Output is exactly the contract's evidence map — C1, C2, C3, C4 each labeled supported-provisionally, contradicted, ambiguous, or missing, plus raised confound flags, attempts, assistance (none), exposure identities consumed (EX-EQGROUPS-DOTS-4x6, EX-ARRAY-GRID-3x7, EX-EQUATION-MATCH-5x3, EX-REFERENT-SWAP-2x8, each single-use and now retired), friction events, and completion status. No mastery, proficiency, grade-level, or preference claim is produced by this instrument under any outcome combination, including four correct responses; no instructional plan is emitted."
